original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-multicross-gorenstein-is-nodal}
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $X$ be a reduced algebraic
$1$-dimensional $k$-scheme. Let $x \in X$ be a multicross singularity
(Definition \ref{definition-multicross}).
If $X$ is Gorenstein, then $x$ is a node.

final_content.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For algebraically closed $k$, a multicross singularity at a closed point $x$ on a one-dimensional $k$-scheme means that $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\{(f_1,\ldots,f_n)\in k[[t]]^n:f_1(0)=\cdots=f_n(0)\}$ for some $n\ge2$, equivalently $k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]/(x_ix_j,\ i\ne j)$. A node is the special case $n=2$. A one-dimensional reduced local ring has $\delta$-invariant $\operatorname{length}(\overline A/A)$, where $\overline A$ is its normalization, and its number of branches is the number of maximal ideals of the normalization of its completed local ring.

$1$-dimensional $k$-scheme. Let $x \in X$ be a multicross singularity
(as defined by the multicross completed-local-ring model above).
If $X$ is Gorenstein, then $x$ is a node.
